what_its_for: Omalizumab is used to treat moderate to severe asthma that is caused by allergies and is not well controlled with inhaled steroids. It is also used to treat chronic hives (itchy skin bumps) that do not go away with antihistamines. It works by blocking a protein in your body called IgE, which triggers allergic reactions and inflammation.
how_to_take: Omalizumab is given as an injection under your skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in the upper arm, thigh, or belly. A healthcare provider will give you this injection at a clinic or doctor's office. You will need to stay at the office for at least 30 minutes after each injection so staff can watch for serious allergic reactions. Do not try to inject this medication at home unless your doctor specifically trains and instructs you to do so.
dosing: Your dose and how often you receive injections depends on your body weight and your allergy test results (IgE levels). Most patients receive injections every 2 to 4 weeks. Common doses range from 75 mg to 375 mg per visit. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose that is right for you. Never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a scheduled injection appointment, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule. Try not to miss appointments, as this can make your asthma or hives harder to control. Do not try to double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Omalizumab is stored in a refrigerator at your doctor's office or pharmacy. It should be kept at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). It should never be frozen. Keep it away from light. If you are self-injecting at home, store vials or pre-filled syringes in the refrigerator. Once removed from the refrigerator, use within 4 hours if kept at room temperature. Do not use if the medication looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles in it.
what_to_avoid: Do not stop taking your other asthma medications (like inhaled steroids or rescue inhalers) unless your doctor tells you to, even if you feel better. Do not use omalizumab to treat a sudden asthma attack or severe allergic reaction — it does not work fast enough for emergencies. Always carry a rescue inhaler with you. Avoid known allergy triggers such as pet dander, dust, mold, and pollen as much as possible.
when_to_call_doctor: Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room right away if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) such as: difficulty breathing, tightening of the chest or throat, swelling of the lips, tongue, or face, dizziness, or fainting. These reactions can happen within minutes OR up to several days after your injection. Contact your doctor if you notice: new or worsening chest pain, unusual bruising or bleeding, signs of infection (fever, chills), severe rash, or if your asthma or hives are getting worse instead of better.
when_it_works: Omalizumab does not work right away. For asthma, it may take 12 to 16 weeks (about 3 to 4 months) before you notice significant improvement. For chronic hives, some people see improvement within a few weeks, but it may take up to 6 months for the full benefit. Be patient and keep all of your appointments even if you do not feel better right away.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Omalizumab should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. It may pass into breast milk, so talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Children: Omalizumab is approved for children 6 years and older for allergic asthma, and for children 12 years and older for chronic hives. Doses are adjusted based on the child's weight. Elderly Patients: Older adults can use this medication, but may need to be monitored more closely for side effects.
